_comment: What the player's AI is asked, when they connect one in Settings (see docs/modding.md, "ai"). Every mod's
ai/prompts.json goes over the ones before it key by key: a mod changes the persona or one prompt without repeating the rest.
persona: who the AI is, sent as the system prompt with every request (a text, or a list of lines joined with spaces).
prompts: one per use, each { prompt, maxLength (characters kept, cut at a sentence or a word), maxTokens, temperature,
lines (the first lines of the answer kept, 1 by default; 0 keeps all) }.
The game always has its own words first; the AI tells them again or adds to them, and a failure leaves the game's own.
{placeholders} are filled like the game's text (money and units as there: {price:money}, {mileage:distance}).
Every prompt may name {language} (the player's language, by its own name), {units} and {title}; the persona does.
The core has only the plain persona and the Settings test: every other use (below) is a setting's, which gives
the AI its voice and its prompts. A use no mod has is not asked: the game keeps its own words.
talk: a rival's line. {line} the game's own line; {name}, {nickname}, {age}, {aggression} (0-100), {temper},
{standing}, {boss}, {moment} (OpponentSelected, TrackSelected, BetTypeChanged, PulledUp), {pinkSlip}, {grudge},
{track}, {car} (the rival's), {playerCar}, {biography}.
street_talk: a line of the diner's word on the street. {line}.
news: a piece in the paper, answered as the headline on the first line and the body after. {headline}, {body}.
ad: an ad's blurb made livelier. {kind} (car, part), {blurb} (the game's own), and the facts the ad hands over.
portrait_look: how a new rival looks, for ComfyUI's picture (comfy_portrait.json's {look}); in English, whatever
the player's language, as image models read English. {name}, {nickname}, {age}, {sex}, {biography}, {aggression}.
test: the Settings screen's Test button.
chat_seller, chat_salesman, chat_rival, chat_buyer: talking to people (chat_buyer: whoever answered the player's own car ad;
a rival who did talks with chat_rival, the fact sheet saying they are buying). Sent after the persona as the rest of who the AI is, with
the talk so far as the messages (the player's, and [what happens] in brackets). {name}, {nickname} (rivals), {age},
{sex}, {temperament} (ai/people.json's words), {place} (text chat.place.*), {player}, {examples} (the prompt's own
"examples", [{ player, answer }], written out under text chat.examples: how the person might talk), {facts}: the game's fact
sheet (text chat.fact.*, chat.deal.*), every turn. Prices are the game's: the sheet says what to answer an offer.
chat_clerk: a part shop's clerk, as the chat prompts; the facts hold the shop and what the game found in its stock for the
player's last ask (text chat.fact.stock.*). clerk_search: the player's ask read as a search of the stock, answered as JSON
(asks, kind, fits, maxPrice, words, want; a provider that can is held to the schema): {said}, {talk} (the last turns), {kinds}
(the kinds in stock), {player}. The game searches the real stock with it; the clerk then talks about what it found.
chat_memory: what a person keeps of a talk, a short note. {name}, {player}, {talk} (the talk written out).
chat_summary: the start of a long talk summed up, once its turns are no longer sent (rules ai.talk.summaryTurns).
{name}, {player}, {earlier} (the summary so far, or nothing), {talk} (the turns to add, written out).
persona: You write for {title}, a street racing game.
Never mention that this is a game, never explain, never add notes or quotation marks.
Keep every name, car, number and fact you are given exactly as given, and invent none about them.
Write in {language}. Speeds, distances and fuel in {units}.

test.prompt: Greet a newcomer in one short sentence.
